scope: Independent source-backed ordering finding only; not a normative global plan review or implementation/acceptance verdict.
severity: major plan sequencing defect if Step3 activates the repository in the running app

evidence.observation: get_settings returns owned AppSettings without revision/provenance and currently reads cached plugin store; migration/default/provider normalization also calls store.set.

write_settings accepts entire owned AppSettings, returns unit, and replaces settings wholesale through plugin store. No field intent, base snapshot identity, expected revision, or patch reaches this boundary. No distinct settings_store function exists in this source: SETTINGS_STORE_PATH and these StoreExt calls own access.
set_log_level reads full snapshot, changes one log_level field and passes entire snapshot to write_settings.
update_microphone_mode independently reads full snapshot, changes always_on_microphone and passes entire snapshot to write_settings.

Architecture requires patch against fresh loaded state. Step3 nevertheless adopts service in settings.rs and removes settings-file plugin ownership/autosave/exit-save before Step4 replaces snapshot writers. Step3 no-lost-fields/no-stale-cache success criterion cannot be guaranteed under that transitional app adoption.
Global plugin-store remains registered; bounded handoff must remove only settings_store.json participation, retaining other stores.

reasoning: Suppose both current writers read base {log:L0,microphone:M0}. Microphone writer commits M1. Log writer then submits {log:L1,microphone:M0}. A lock/reload adapter diffing that submitted snapshot against latest durable state sees L1 and M0 as changes; the interface cannot distinguish stale M0 from an intentional microphone reset. Reload and write serialization alone do not reconstruct intent. A global cached baseline would add unspecified state and still is not this interface contract. Removing plugin settings-file ownership without changing these writers also leaves their current write boundary incoherent; retaining it alongside a repository would retain independent cached rewrites. This is a source-backed feasible interleaving, not an observed runtime loss or a claim about uninspected plugin autosave defaults.

Gate no direct writer/cache flush remaining and live application startup/write race evidence on that atomic cutover.
